#
# The Verdin iMX95's display registers under its own Linux, read by the
# owner's session on 2026-11-25 with devmem2 (one 32-bit read each, nothing
# written) while the Toradex Capacitive Touch Display 10.1" LVDS on the
# Mallow's X12 showed Toradex's Qt demo.
#
# Module "Toradex Verdin iMX95 WB", 8 GB; Toradex Reference Multimedia Image
# "TDX Wayland with XWayland 7.8.0+build.17 (scarthgap)", kernel
# 6.6.157-7.8.0; overlays verdin-imx95_panel-cap-touch-10inch-lvds_overlay.dtbo
# and verdin-imx95_spidev_overlay.dtbo.
# Connector card0-LVDS-1 connected and enabled, 1280x800.
# Clocks (clk_summary): ldbpll_vco 2986200000, ldbpll 497700000,
# ldb_phy_div 497700000, lvds_ch0_gate on, lvds_ch1_gate off,
# ldb_pll_div7 71100000, lvds_di0_gate on, lvds_di1_gate off, disp1pix
# 24000000 (no user), dispapb 133333333, dispocram 400000000, dispaxi
# 800000000. Power domains display and camera on.
# Backlight: platform/42500000.pwm channel 0 "backlight-lvds-native", period
# 6666667 ns, duty 3111111 ns, polarity inverse, brightness 4 of 7.
#
# Format: ADDRESS WIDTH VALUE (hex, 32, hex), in the order the words were
# read. A word whose single read killed the reading process (SIGBUS; the
# board went on running) is a "# ADDRESS FAULT" line: each is a write-only
# register or a reserved word of hal_nxp's PERI_DISPLAY_SEERIS.h, and the
# read list (imx95-display-allow.txt) leaves it out.
# The decode is driver/docs/imx95-display.md, section 6 ("What the board
# showed").
#
# LVDS CSR (LDB)
0x4b0c0000 32 0x00000014
0x4b0c0004 32 0x00082221
0x4b0c0008 32 0x00001075
0x4b0c000c 32 0x00000000
